data.narrative:
Kraken Robotics is a public-stage company operating in Defense & Security. The comparable universe consists of 2 public peers (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private peers, including Evolv Technology, Anduril Industries, Helsing, Castelion, and Shield AI. This represents a narrow peer set within a 26-company Defense & Security sector, reflecting the specialized nature of frontier robotics markets.

The peer-median method is not applicable here. Of the 26 same-sector peers identified, fewer than 3 companies meet narrow filters for stage alignment and valuation tier comparability. Applying an all-sector median would introduce material distortion given the heterogeneity of Defense & Security subsegments and the distinct technical and commercialization profiles of robotics versus other defense verticals. This constraint limits confidence in traditional comparable-company multiples.

Without sufficient narrow peer clustering, triangulation across methods cannot be completed at this stage. A robust valuation would require either: (1) expansion to adjacent aerospace/autonomy sectors with similar technology risk and procurement dynamics, or (2) income-based approaches anchored to contract pipeline and gross margin visibility. The 2 public comps warrant individual analysis (revenue multiples, growth rates), but broader sector multiples should not be applied as proxy. Key uncertainties include customer concentration risk, government contract sustainability, and the development timeline for core robotics platforms relative to Defense & Security budget cycles.
